# Road map "codec-export" — AV1 and VP9 export with bundled encoders (#377)

**Opened 2026-10-27** (C0), in the worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` on branch `codecs`, from
`75fd806`; each phase is gated and merged into main alone (CX-11). This road map's decisions are
CX-1 onwards, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`. Its brief is issue #377; the
acknowledgements its licences feed are #376.

## Goal

Frame Job exports H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all
through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. After this road map it also exports AV1 and VP9, encoded
by two libraries built into the app (SVT-AV1 and libvpx), into MP4 or WebM, with Opus audio in
WebM and alpha in VP9 WebM.

## The owner's choices

**2026-10-27** (the brief, `request.md`; binding; "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the
encoders."):

- **AV1 encoder: SVT-AV1 only** (pinned v4.2.0). There is no libaom.
  - Three speed choices on the export sheet: Faster = preset 8, Balanced = preset 6 (default),
    Smaller file = preset 4.
- **VP9 encoder: libvpx** (pinned v1.17.0), one speed (cpu-used 4, row-mt).
- **Export rows:** all four of these. VP9-in-MP4 is NOT wanted.
  - AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
  - AV1 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 + alpha in WebM.
- **WebM writer:** a Rust Matroska/WebM writer in `core/`, next to the import reader, not
  libwebm. Writing container bytes is not sample work, under the precedent of #216-R's reader.

Also the owner's, standing: only higher-quality exports matter (2026-10-27); no feature size
budget; memory limits relative to physical RAM; person-only checks go in
`docs/manual-checks.md`.

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Opus:** macOS AudioToolbox's Opus encoder, not libopus, after the mix and loudness gain
  (CX-7). *The owner can change this.*
- **HDR:** AV1 at 10 bits with HLG/PQ, plus HDR10 mastering metadata, on the AV1 rows; VP9
  Profile 2 HDR later, WebM only, in its own phase (CX-8). *The owner can change this.*
- **Library sources:** pinned tarballs checked by SHA-256, fetched and built by `make codecs`
  and cached by a stamp; no sources vendored into the repo (CX-5). *The owner can change this.*
- **Rate model:** the bitrate semantics kept on every row, the efficiency spent on the picture
  (CX-9). *The owner can change this.*
- **AV1 decode on M1/M2:** the export works there, but Frame Job cannot preview or re-import
  its own AV1 file; the guide says so (CX-10). *The owner can change this.*
- **The encoders platform-side** (CX-4) and **the working arrangement** (CX-11). *The owner can
  change these.*

## How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)

- **The export table.** `core/src/export_table.rs` (584) holds each row: `id`, `codec`, the
  container, and `avf_preset` (`None` today means the ImageIO still writer). C1 adds a writer
  field for the encoder rows rather than overloading `avf_preset: None`. `export.rs` (259),
  `export_size.rs` (274) and `export_overrides.rs` (295) are the rest of the settings.
- **The writer.** `app/Sources/ExporterWriter.swift` (586) runs an
  `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` of 64RGBAHalf frames into a pump on `videoQueue`;
  `ExporterWriter+Settings.swift` (468) holds `defaultVideoBitrate` (0.07 bits/pixel/frame) and
  the Quality tiers; `+Chapters` (248) the chapters. `Exporter.swift` (598) is at the cap, and
  the encoder path goes in new files. The audio pump reads 48 kHz stereo and gains it once
  (`ExporterAudioGain.swift`, `ExporterLoudness.swift`); `ExportAudioEnd.swift` holds #337's
  length rule.
- **The reader the WebM writer mirrors.** `core/src/container*.rs` (seven files, 2,024 lines
  today): EBML, the headers, the blocks, the timing and its grid rule, Vorbis. The writer goes
  in new modules beside them (CX-6).
- **The build.** `make rust` (cargo, then `project.yml`'s "Build Rust Core" pre-build step) is
  the shape `make codecs` copies (CX-5). `tools/proof/gate.py` stamps each Full step by its
  inputs and tool versions; `tools/proof/swift_build.py` is the one probe build line;
  `tools/proof/tree_copy.py` builds old or mutated trees in copies.
- **The bridge.** `app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h` imports only the core's header
  today. The encoders' headers join it (CX-4); no `rc_*` export wraps them.

## Phases

- **C0 — decisions and the encoder build; CX-1..CX-11.** CX-1..CX-11 recorded in §11 before
  any code, and this road map with the spike's record. `tools/codecs/build_codecs.py` fetches
  SVT-AV1 v4.2.0 and libvpx v1.17.0 as pinned tarballs, checks each by SHA-256, builds them
  arm64, static and encoder-only at the app's deployment target (26.0), and installs headers,
  archives and licence texts into `build/codecs/`, reused by its stamp. `make codecs`; `app`,
  `app-debug`, `typecheck` and `test` depend on it; `project.yml`'s "Build Codecs" pre-build
  step, the header search path, both archives by full path in every configuration's
  `OTHER_LDFLAGS`, and "Copy Codec Licences" into `Contents/Resources/Licenses/`. One Swift
  file, `CodecLibraries.swift`, reads each library's version and opens an SVT-AV1 handle, behind
  `-RCCodecProbe 1`. The gate, the probe builder, the tree copies, the four spikes' own build
  lines and the publish workflow's cmake. **Acceptance:** `make gate` passes; `dist_check`
  41/41 with a stand-in Sparkle key (D36–D41: the encoder symbols in both executables, no load
  command outside the system and Sparkle, the licences byte-identical in both bundles), its
  mutants 34/34; `build_codecs.py --selftest` and its three mutants; tree_copy's T6.
  **Proof:** `tools/proof/codecs_proof.py` (L1–L3) against Release.
- **C1 — AV1 in MP4 (SVT-AV1), 8-bit.** The row (`av1`, MP4, AAC) and its Speed popup
  (Faster / Balanced / Smaller file, CX-2) on the export sheet and in `export`'s MCP mirror;
  a writer field in the export table instead of overloading `avf_preset: None`; the Metal
  conversion from the compositor's 64RGBAHalf to planar I420 (BT.709, video range); a dedicated
  serial encode queue owning the encoder, with progress counted by frames submitted, the
  existing cancel flag checked per frame by the pump and the queue, and the flush before
  `markAsFinished`; the packets into a passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` with a
  `CMVideoFormatDescription` holding `av1C` (built in the core from the sequence header OBU);
  temporal delimiters stripped; the `ftyp` patched to carry `av01`; the rate model (CX-9) and
  its re-measurement on a full-length export; the guide page with CX-10's sentence.
  **Acceptance and proof:** ffprobe reads `av1`/`av01` with AAC beside it; ffmpeg decodes every
  frame and the count is the range's; `export_offset_proof`'s clicks land; cancel leaves no
  file; a manual-checks row for playback on an M3 or later.
- **C2 — AV1 10-bit and HDR.** The I010 path; HLG/PQ tagged in the sequence header and in
  `colr`; HD-5's `mdcv`/`clli`; `dynamic_range`'s rules on the row as `hevc_10bit` has them
  (CX-8). **Acceptance and proof:** ffprobe reads `yuv420p10le`, the transfer and primaries,
  and the mastering and light-level side data, for HLG, PQ and SDR; the SDR version export.
- **C3 — the WebM writer and Opus.** The core's EBML writer (`rc_webm_*`: open, add a packet,
  finish), with Cues, chapters, the range, the size and #337's audio length; Opus from
  AudioToolbox through a 960-frame FIFO, OpusHead and CodecDelay built from `primeInfo` (CX-7);
  AV1 in WebM. **Acceptance and proof:** core tests that write and re-read through the #216-R
  reader (codecs, `av1C`, colour, OpusHead, timing on the grid rule, chapters); ffmpeg decodes
  the file with zero errors; Frame Job re-imports it on a Mac that decodes AV1.
- **C4 — VP9 (libvpx) in WebM**, 8-bit, then Profile 2 HDR with the container's `Colour` and
  MasteringMetadata (CX-3, CX-8). **Acceptance and proof:** as C3, for `vp9`; Frame Job
  re-imports and previews its own VP9 WebM on any Apple silicon Mac.
- **C5 — VP9 with alpha in WebM.** A second libvpx instance for the alpha plane, frame-aligned,
  as BlockAdditional 1 with `AlphaMode`; G-35's straight alpha and the shape rule.
  **Acceptance and proof:** the libvpx decoder's alpha against the source's (the spike's PSNR
  method); manual-checks rows for Chrome and Firefox.
- **C6 — 4K and memory.** 4K measured on every row; the export queue's limit on concurrent
  encoder jobs, relative to physical RAM; the sheet's time estimate. **Acceptance and proof:**
  the measurements recorded here, and the limit's rule in §11.

## S — the spike

3	/// The export queue (road map 2's phase 7e): the exports a person has
4	/// confirmed but does not want to sit and watch, run one after another while
5	/// the editor stays live.
6	///
7	/// **There is no AppKit in this file, and that is the design rather than
8	/// tidiness.** A queue window can be checked by neither of this project's two
9	/// instruments: the offscreen harness renders an `EditorViewController` into a
10	/// window and nothing else, and MCP drives the app through tools — and the
11	/// agent's `export` enqueues here, so a tool reaches this list but never the
12	/// window (below, spec §11 #326). What a proof CAN do is
13	/// compile a probe out of the whole of `app/Sources`
14	/// (`tools/proof/phase6_chrome.py`'s `build_probe`), make one of these,
15	/// enqueue two jobs, spin the main run loop until `isIdle` and read `jobs`
16	/// back — without an `NSWindow` ever being ordered front. So the job list and
17	/// its state machine live here, where a script can reach them, and
18	/// `ExportQueueWindowController.swift` is a READER of this and nothing else:
19	/// it holds no job, decides nothing, and closing it stops nothing.
20	/// `AudioNormalize.swift` and `CaptionLayout.swift` are the same split — the
21	/// arithmetic where a script can call it, the dialog around it — and phase 5's
22	/// level meter is the closest sibling, where the MODEL publishes a number
23	/// precisely so that a proof need not photograph a window.
24	///
25	/// **The agent's `export` is a job here (spec §11 #326).** It keeps its
26	/// refusals synchronous, then enqueues exactly as Add to Queue does and
27	/// answers the job's id at once; `export_status` follows the job and
28	/// `cancel_export` calls `cancel` (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`). The
29	/// queue's own API is unchanged by it: the mirror reads `job(_:)` and
30	/// observes `didChangeNotification` like the window does, and no tool
31	/// exists for a person's own queued job.
32	///
33	/// **One job at a time, on the MAIN thread, a fresh `Exporter` for each.**
34	/// `Exporter.export`'s own doc says main-thread-only and one export at a time,
35	/// and it means both: it schedules a run-loop `Timer` — which must be
36	/// invalidated on the thread it was scheduled on — and calls its progress and
37	/// completion handlers on the main thread. So this is a CHAIN and not a pool:
38	/// `start()` runs the head of the list and each completion runs the next. A
39	/// `DispatchQueue` of exporters would be the wrong shape whatever the machine's
40	/// core count, and not only because of the timer — an `Exporter` carries
41	/// per-export state (`recipeKey`, `cancelRequested`, the loudness scratch
42	/// buffer), which is why each job gets its own rather than one being reset
43	/// between jobs. Every method below is main-thread-only for that reason, like
44	/// the exporter it drives.
45	///
46	/// **What a job holds is the whole of what it will write, captured when it was
47	/// confirmed.** The `ReelProject` is a handle and handles are immutable (spec
48	/// §5.5) — every edit and every undo makes a NEW one — so a queued write cannot
49	/// be reached by an edit made after it, and it needs no clone: `Exporter.export`
50	/// publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key it mints for itself, never the
51	/// document's, so even the frames the compositor serves this export come from
52	/// this handle. The document may be edited, undone or CLOSED while the job
53	/// waits; the handle is retained here and the Rust project behind it lives
54	/// until the job is gone.
55	///
56	/// **And the media URLs are resolved at ENQUEUE, which is what makes them part
57	/// of that same snapshot.** `ProjectDocument.mediaURLs()` resolves a bookmark
58	/// and asks the filesystem whether the file is there (`mediaURL(for:)`), so it
59	/// is a reading of the disk at the moment it is called: resolving at RUN time
60	/// would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after the job was
61	/// queued, which is the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. That
62	/// rule is structural here rather than remembered — `enqueue` takes a
63	/// `[UInt32: URL]` and a job holds no document, so there is nothing to ask
64	/// again later even if somebody wanted to.
65	///
66	/// **The REVERSE resolution is the third thing in that snapshot, and it was
67	/// missing.** Handle immutability covers the project and nothing beside it:
68	/// which clips play from a pre-rendered backwards file is a reading of the
69	/// disk too (`ProjectDocument.reverseState`, `ReverseCache.existing`), it
70	/// cannot be derived from a bare handle, and it lives in a side table keyed by
71	/// object IDENTITY — which the document overwrites on every edit and removes
72	/// when it closes. So a job queued from a timeline holding a reversed clip
73	/// used to answer `.none` the moment anything was edited, and `.none` means
74	/// "not reversed": the export took the forward asset at the mirrored source
75	/// window, unslated and unreported. It is captured here at enqueue, exactly as
76	/// the URLs are, and PINNED to this job's own handle for the length of its
77	/// write (`ReverseSource.pin`). Anything else the picture depends on that is
78	/// neither in the handle nor derivable from it joins that list.
79	final class ExportQueueController {
80	    /// The app's one queue: the export sheet's Add to Queue fills it and
81	    /// Window ▸ Export Queue shows it.
82	    static let shared = ExportQueueController()
83	
84	    /// Where a job is. A closed set with no associated values, so the two
85	    /// readers ask it different questions without either having to spell a
86	    /// message: the window's row draws its own wording (which carries a
87	    /// percentage the state cannot know), and a probe compares the case and
88	    /// reads `Job.message` for the sentence. The raw values are the same
89	    /// strings a probe writes into its JSON answer.
90	    enum State: String {
91	        /// Queued and not started. The only state a job can be enqueued in.
92	        case waiting
93	        /// The one job an `Exporter` is running. At most one at any moment.
94	        case running
95	        /// The file landed.
96	        case completed
97	        /// Stopped by a person, either before it started or mid-write — in
98	        /// which case its half-written file has been removed.
99	        case cancelled
100	        /// The exporter refused or failed. Whatever it had written is LEFT on
101	        /// disk, which is `ExportProgressSheetController`'s posture and not a
102	        /// new one: a cancel is a person saying "not this", where a failure is
103	        /// evidence, and the file names itself in the message.
104	        case failed
105	
106	        /// Whether the job is over, however it ended — the test for "may be
107	        /// removed from the list" and for "no longer holds a project handle
108	        /// worth keeping".
109	        var isFinished: Bool { self == .completed || self == .cancelled || self == .failed }
110	    }
111	
112	    /// One confirmed export. Everything it needs was read when it was
113	    /// enqueued; see the type doc for why that is the whole point of it.
114	    struct Job {
115	        /// Monotonic within one launch. The window's rows and every method
116	        /// below address a job by this rather than by index, because a job can
117	        /// be removed from the middle of the list while a later one runs.
118	        let id: UInt64
119	        /// The timeline as it was confirmed — immutable, and retained here, so
120	        /// the document behind it may be edited, undone or closed.
121	        ///
122	        /// A FINISHED job goes on holding it, and that is a real cost stated
123	        /// rather than hidden: a handle is the project's model and not its
124	        /// media, so it is JSON-sized, and Clear Finished (or Remove) is what
125	        /// releases it along with the row that says where the file went.
126	        /// Dropping the handle at the finish would buy those bytes back and
127	        /// cost the field its `let` — an immutable job whose contents change
128	        /// once is a harder thing to reason about than a list somebody tidies.
129	        let project: ReelProject
130	        /// The media files as they resolved AT ENQUEUE.
131	        let urls: [UInt32: URL]
132	        /// Which of this timeline's clips play from a pre-rendered backwards
133	        /// file, as that resolved AT ENQUEUE — the type doc's third piece of
134	        /// the snapshot. Read from `ReverseSource` here and published back to
135	        /// it under this job's own handle while the job runs, because the
136	        /// document's copy is overwritten by the next edit and dropped when it
137	        /// closes.
138	        let reverse: ReverseResolution
139	        let settings: ExportSettings
140	        let destination: URL
141	        /// What this export asks of the PICTURE besides the timeline — the
142	        /// burn-in (`RecipeOptions`). Carried per job, because two jobs from

144	        let options: RecipeOptions

146	        /// the type doc's list again: a module saved after Add to Queue is not
147	        /// in the handle, and the document's set is swapped by that save and
148	        /// dropped when it closes. `Exporter.export` pins it for the write.
149	        let graphics: GraphicSet?
150	        var state: State = .waiting
151	        /// 0…1, and only meaningful while `state` is `.running`.
152	        var progress: Double = 0
153	        /// The line a person reads when it is over: what was written and what
154	        /// the file measured, or why it stopped — plus the one thing worth
155	        /// saying mid-flight, that a cancel is in hand. nil while it waits.
156	        var message: String?
157	        /// What the exporter says it is doing right now, or nil for "writing",
158	        /// which is the caller's own wording. Today the only phase is the
159	        /// loudness measurement, which on an audio-only export is half the wait
160	        /// and the half where nothing is on disk yet.
161	        ///
162	        /// A field of its own rather than a use of `message`, because the two
163	        /// are written by different things at the same time: the progress tick
164	        /// arrives ten times a second and would otherwise wipe the "Stopping…"
165	        /// a person had just asked for.
166	        var phase: String?
167	        /// Set on a COMPLETED job when a later job starts writing to the same
168	        /// path, because from that moment this row's file is not this row's
169	        /// any more — `Exporter.startWriting` removes whatever is at the
170	        /// destination before it builds its pipeline, so the earlier export is
171	        /// gone whether the later one succeeds, fails or is cancelled.
172	        ///
173	        /// The row stops claiming "Exported …" and stops offering Show in
174	        /// Finder. It is a fact about what happened rather than a state: the
175	        /// job really did complete, and rewriting its `state` would lose that.
176	        ///
177	        /// One case marks it where the file in fact survives, and it is the
178	        /// honest direction of the two: a later job whose COMPOSITION fails to
179	        /// build returns before the delete, so nothing was destroyed. It is
180	        /// left alone rather than reached for, because knowing which failures
181	        /// precede the delete means reading `Exporter`'s stages from here, and
182	        /// a shared destination implies a shared project — a build that failed
183	        /// for job 2 would almost always have failed for job 1.
184	        var superseded: Bool = false
185	        /// What the graphics warned while a COMPLETED job's file was drawn
186	        /// (G-24 (c)): the row's count and its tooltip's list.
187	        var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning] = []
188	        /// What a COMPLETED job's sound measured, read off its exporter at the
189	        /// finish — the figures the row's message summarises, kept whole for
190	        /// `export_status`'s `loudness` (spec §11 #326). nil otherwise.
191	        var loudness: ExportLoudness? = nil
192	
193	        /// What the row calls this job. The file name and not the path: the
194	        /// row is narrow, and the full path is the tooltip's job.
195	        var name: String { destination.lastPathComponent }
196	    }
197	
198	    /// Posted after any change to `jobs` — an enqueue, a progress tick, a
199	    /// finish, a cancel, a removal — with the controller as the `object`, so
200	    /// an observer of the shared queue is never woken by a probe's own
201	    /// instance. Main thread, like everything else here.
202	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
203	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportQueueDidChange")
204	
205	    /// Every job this launch still knows about, in the order they were added.
206	    /// A finished one stays until it is removed, because "it is done and here
207	    /// is where it went" is the queue's other job.
208	    private(set) var jobs: [Job] = []
209	
210	    /// The exporter running `runningID`'s job, and nil whenever nothing is
211	    /// running. Set and cleared together with the job's state, so `isIdle` can
212	    /// be answered from `jobs` alone.
213	    private var exporter: Exporter?
214	
215	    /// The handle whose reverse resolution is pinned in `ReverseSource` right
216	    /// now — the running job's, and nil whenever nothing is running. Held
217	    /// separately from the job so that `launch` and `finished` are provably one
218	    /// pin and one release, whatever happens to the list in between.
219	    private var pinnedProject: ReelProject?
220	
221	    /// True only while `start()` is inside `Exporter.export`. An early refusal
222	    /// — `noPlan`, `emptyTimeline` — completes SYNCHRONOUSLY, so `finished`

224	    /// would be launched from inside the previous one's stack frame and a
225	    /// queue of refusals would recurse as deep as it is long. With it, a
226	    /// re-entrant `start()` is refused and the frame already on the stack

230	    private var nextID: UInt64 = 1

312	    /// and safe to call at any time: `enqueue` calls it, every completion

358	        didChange()
359	        exporter.export(
360	            project: job.project, urls: job.urls, settings: job.settings, to: job.destination,
361	            options: job.options, graphics: job.graphics,
362	            progress: { [weak self] value in self?.progressed(job.id, value) },
363	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.finished(job.id, result) })
364	    }
365	
366	    private func progressed(_ id: UInt64, _ value: Double) {
367	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
368	            jobs[index].state == .running
369	        else { return }
370	        jobs[index].progress = min(max(value, 0), 1)
371	        // The exporter names its own phase while it has one. The progress
372	        // sheet asks the same question with the same call; a row that said
373	        // "Writing" through the measurement would be claiming a file that does
374	        // not exist yet.
375	        jobs[index].phase = exporter?.phaseDescription
376	        didChange()
377	    }
378	
379	    /// The one exit for all three outcomes, and the mirror of
380	    /// `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` — deliberately, because there
381	    /// must not be two accounts of what finishing an export means. The
382	    /// exporter is cleared first, so the `start()` at the foot can hand the
383	    /// next job a fresh one.
384	    private func finished(_ id: UInt64, _ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
385	        // Read BEFORE the exporter is dropped: `Exporter.finish` publishes the
386	        // measurement and then calls this, so the report is there now and only
387	        // now.
388	        let report = exporter?.loudnessReport
389	        let measured = report.map { " \($0.summary)." } ?? ""
390	        let warnings = exporter?.graphicWarnings ?? []
391	        exporter = nil
392	        // The pin goes with the exporter, and from `pinnedProject` rather than
393	        // from the job, so that releasing it cannot depend on the job still
394	        // being in the list. Exactly one release per `launch`, which is what
395	        // `ReverseSource.pin` asks for; a pin left behind would retain the
396	        // Rust project for the life of the process.
397	        if let pinned = pinnedProject {
398	            ReverseSource.shared.unpin(pinned)
399	            pinnedProject = nil
400	        }
401	        if let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) {
402	            jobs[index].phase = nil
403	            switch result {
404	            case .success(let url):
405	                jobs[index].state = .completed
406	                jobs[index].progress = 1
407	                jobs[index].graphicWarnings = warnings
408	                jobs[index].loudness = report
409	                // The count BEFORE the loudness figures: the row truncates
410	                // its tail (`ExportQueueRowView`).
411	                jobs[index].message = "Exported “\(url.lastPathComponent)”."
412	                    + Exporter.graphicWarningSuffix(warnings, hover: false) + measured
413	            case .failure(let error):
414	                if case Exporter.ExportError.cancelled = error {
415	                    // A cancelled job leaves nothing behind, and this line is
416	                    // DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than the thing that achieves it
417	                    // — measured, because the obvious reading is wrong and a
418	                    // reader who believes it would be relying on a guarantee
419	                    // this line does not provide. Both pipelines already
420	                    // clean up after themselves: `AVAssetWriter.cancelWriting()`
421	                    // removes its own part-file (`ExporterWriter.swift` says
422	                    // so where it calls it) and `ImageSequenceWriter.report`
423	                    // removes its own. Deleting this line changes no observable
424	                    // outcome — phase 7's proof mutated it away and scored
425	                    // 77/77 — so the check beside it is written as the OUTCOME
426	                    // ("nothing is left behind") and not as a guard on this
427	                    // call. Keep it: it costs nothing, it states the policy
428	                    // where the policy is decided, and it is what holds if a
429	                    // third pipeline ever arrives that is less tidy.
430	                    // `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` is the same line
431	                    // for the same reason.
432	                    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: jobs[index].destination)
433	                    jobs[index].state = .cancelled
434	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
435	                    jobs[index].message = "Cancelled."
436	                } else {
437	                    jobs[index].state = .failed
438	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
439	                    jobs[index].message = error.localizedDescription
440	                }
441	            }
442	        }
443	        didChange()
444	        start()
445	    }
446	
447	    // MARK: - Stopping and tidying
448	
449	    /// Stops one job, whether it has started or not.
450	    ///
451	    /// A WAITING job is simply marked: it has no exporter to stop and no file
452	    /// to remove, because nothing has been written under its name. A RUNNING
453	    /// one is asked to stop and answers through `finished`, which is where its
454	    /// file is removed — one exit, so a cancel from the window and a cancel
455	    /// from a script clean up identically. A finished job is left alone.
456	    func cancel(_ id: UInt64) {
457	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return }
458	        switch jobs[index].state {
459	        case .waiting:
460	            jobs[index].state = .cancelled
461	            jobs[index].message = "Cancelled before it started."
462	            didChange()
463	        case .running:
464	            jobs[index].message = "Stopping…"
465	            exporter?.cancel()
466	            didChange()
467	        case .completed, .cancelled, .failed:
468	            break
469	        }
470	    }
471	
472	    /// Stops everything. The WAITING jobs go first and the running one last,
473	    /// and the order is load-bearing: cancelling the running job posts its
474	    /// completion, and a completion starts the next waiting job — so stopping
475	    /// the writer first would start the very jobs this is meant to stop.
476	    func cancelAll() {
477	        for job in jobs where job.state == .waiting { cancel(job.id) }
478	        if let running = runningJob { cancel(running.id) }
479	    }
480	
481	    /// Drops one finished row. A job still waiting or running is not removed —
482	    /// cancel it first, which is what the window's one button does in its two
483	    /// states.
484	    func remove(_ id: UInt64) {
485	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
486	            jobs[index].state.isFinished
487	        else { return }
488	        jobs.remove(at: index)
489	        didChange()
490	    }
491	
492	    /// Drops every finished row and leaves the queue itself running.
493	    func clearFinished() {
494	        let before = jobs.count
495	        jobs.removeAll { $0.state.isFinished }
496	        if jobs.count != before { didChange() }
497	    }
498	
499	    private func didChange() {
500	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
501	    }
502	}

- **Burn-in is a RECIPE option, never an export override.** It goes through
  `rc_project_frame_recipe_opts`, `RecipeSource` and `renderFrame`, the last because GIF and
  APNG bypass the writer.
  - The layer is appended LAST, so a recipe without the option is byte-identical.
  - It is placed as a fraction of the canvas height.
  - The timecode is non-drop, in PROJECT time.
- **A user preset stores CONTROL CHOICES and never resolved values.** The core never learns about
  presets. The restore order in the sheet is load-bearing.
- **The export queue is a chain run on main with a fresh `Exporter` per job.** Two concurrent
  `Exporter`s deadlock.
  - `mediaURLs()` is captured at enqueue.
  - The controller contains no AppKit.
  - The queue has no MCP mirror, because it edits no project.

Derived, not measured: a minute of 1080p30 (1,800 frames) at these fps is ~24 s with SVT 6,
~12 s SVT 8, ~44 s SVT 4, ~1.9 min libaom good-6, ~8 min libaom good-4, ~46 s VP9 good-4.
The export's compositor time is on top; 4K was not measured (4× the pixels).

#### Recommendation (question 2)

**AV1: SVT-AV1.** Plainly, the numbers argue against libaom as the export encoder despite
the natural pull toward AOM's reference (and the owner's brother's team): at every speed an
export sheet would offer, SVT-AV1 gives more quality for the time.
- Matched quality: SVT 4 ≈ libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF +3.36 vs +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 vs
  +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`, +3.15 vs +3.33/+3.22 at 10-bit) at ~41 fps against 13.6–16 fps:
  about 3× faster.
- Matched speed: at ~100–150 fps SVT 8 gives +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37.
- libaom's best (good-3/4, +4.1–4.2 on `real8`) is ~0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at 2.6–3.7 fps,
  about 11× slower — a 2-minute clip would take ~16 minutes.
- In libaom's favour: a higher worst-frame VMAF (92 vs 88), lower memory (0.5–1.1 GB vs
  1.0–2.1 GB), and it is AOM's reference. SVT-AV1 is also AOMedia's
  (gitlab.com/AOMediaCodec) under the same AOM patent licence.

Presets the sheet should offer for AV1 (SVT-AV1, all 1080p30 on this Mac):

| Row | SVT preset | fps 8-bit / 10-bit | Bitrate for HEVC's quality (real8 / gh5 / real10) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Faster | 8 | ~148 / ~115 | −41 % / −33 % / −32 % |
| Balanced (default) | 6 | ~75 / ~64 | −52 % / −47 % / −44 % |
| Smaller file | 4 | ~41 / ~34 | −58 % / −52 % / −56 % |

Presets 10 and 12 are within 0–0.7 VMAF of HEVC at 2–3× its CPU cost — not worth a row.

**VP9: libvpx** (the only real option), one row at `--good --cpu-used=4 --row-mt=1`
(~39 fps, 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality); good-2 buys +0.14–0.43 VMAF for ~35 % more time; rt-8 is
only HEVC's quality. VP9's reason to exist in the sheet is web playback and alpha, not
efficiency: at matched quality it needs ~1.4–1.7× SVT 6's bitrate (good-4: 3,605 vs 2,144; 2,774 vs 1,989; 3,714 vs 2,452 kbps).

### 3. Containers

#### AV1 in MP4 — yes, AVAssetWriter writes precompressed `av01`
each frame to a **dedicated serial encode queue** owning the encoder (libaom/libvpx encode
synchronously with internal lag; SVT is send/receive with its own threads). Encoded packets
go to the passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (MP4) or the WebM writer. Progress: frames
submitted (the encoder's lag, 25–35 frames, is under a second at 30 fps); a final flush
(`encode(NULL)` / SVT EOS) before `markAsFinished`. Cancel: the existing flag, checked per
frame by both pump and encode queue, then the encoder destroyed after `allInputsFinished`,
as G3c requires for the reader. Back-pressure is natural: the pump's
`isReadyForMoreMediaData` loop blocks on a bounded queue to the encoder.

Memory: one compositor frame is 16,588,800 B; I420 3,110,400 B; I010 6,220,800 B. Encoder
RSS measured above: SVT-AV1 1.0–2.1 GB at 1080p (most at preset 4 and 10-bit), libaom
0.5–1.1 GB, libvpx 0.3–0.5 GB. SVT's thread/buffer count follows `--lp`; 4K will be larger
(not measured).

### 7. HDR

| | HEVC rows today | AV1 | VP9 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Profile | Main 10 | Main (profile 0), 10-bit | Profile 2 |
| Colour in the bitstream | VUI | sequence header `color_config`: `AV1E_SET_COLOR_PRIMARIES/TRANSFER_CHARACTERISTICS/MATRIX_COEFFICIENTS` (libaom), `color_primaries`/`transfer_characteristics` in SVT's config — measured: aomenc `--transfer-characteristics=hlg` gave an MP4 ffprobe reads as `arib-std-b67` with no container tags | only `color_space` (BT.709/BT.2020…, `VP9E_SET_COLOR_SPACE`), **no transfer** — HLG/PQ must come from the container |
| MP4 tags | `colr` from `AVVideoColorPropertiesKey` | `colr` from the description's extensions — measured HLG and PQ | `vpcC` carries primaries/transfer/matrix — measured HLG |
| HDR10 metadata (HD-5's fixed values) | VT compression keys | `mdcv`/`clli` boxes from `MasteringDisplayColorVolume`/`ContentLightLevelInfo` extensions — measured written and read back; in-band metadata OBUs available (`aom_img_add_metadata` with `OBU_METADATA_TYPE_HDR_MDCV/CLL`, SVT `mastering_display`/`content_light_level`), not exercised; AV1-ISOBMFF says the boxes SHOULD be present and SHALL equal the OBUs | MP4 boxes as for AV1; WebM `Colour/MasteringMetadata` + `MaxCLL`/`MaxFALL` — measured with libwebm and read back by the core |
| WebM tags | — | `Colour` element — measured HLG | `Colour` element — measured PQ |

So the new 10-bit rows can take `hevc_10bit`'s place in H-3's rules (`"hdr": true`,
`dynamic_range` hlg/pq/sdr), with the tags written in both the bitstream (AV1) and the
container. No Dolby Vision question arises. Not measured: any player's HDR rendering of
these files.

#### Recommendation (question 2)

**AV1: SVT-AV1.** Plainly, the numbers argue against libaom as the export encoder despite
the natural pull toward AOM's reference (and the owner's brother's team): at every speed an
export sheet would offer, SVT-AV1 gives more quality for the time.
- Matched quality: SVT 4 ≈ libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF +3.36 vs +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 vs
  +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`, +3.15 vs +3.33/+3.22 at 10-bit) at ~41 fps against 13.6–16 fps:
  about 3× faster.
- Matched speed: at ~100–150 fps SVT 8 gives +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37.
- libaom's best (good-3/4, +4.1–4.2 on `real8`) is ~0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at 2.6–3.7 fps,
  about 11× slower — a 2-minute clip would take ~16 minutes.
- In libaom's favour: a higher worst-frame VMAF (92 vs 88), lower memory (0.5–1.1 GB vs
  1.0–2.1 GB), and it is AOM's reference. SVT-AV1 is also AOMedia's
  (gitlab.com/AOMediaCodec) under the same AOM patent licence.

Presets the sheet should offer for AV1 (SVT-AV1, all 1080p30 on this Mac):

| Row | SVT preset | fps 8-bit / 10-bit | Bitrate for HEVC's quality (real8 / gh5 / real10) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Faster | 8 | ~148 / ~115 | −41 % / −33 % / −32 % |
| Balanced (default) | 6 | ~75 / ~64 | −52 % / −47 % / −44 % |
| Smaller file | 4 | ~41 / ~34 | −58 % / −52 % / −56 % |

Presets 10 and 12 are within 0–0.7 VMAF of HEVC at 2–3× its CPU cost — not worth a row.

**VP9: libvpx** (the only real option), one row at `--good --cpu-used=4 --row-mt=1`
(~39 fps, 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality); good-2 buys +0.14–0.43 VMAF for ~35 % more time; rt-8 is
only HEVC's quality. VP9's reason to exist in the sheet is web playback and alpha, not
efficiency: at matched quality it needs ~1.4–1.7× SVT 6's bitrate (good-4: 3,605 vs 2,144; 2,774 vs 1,989; 3,714 vs 2,452 kbps).

### 3. Containers

#### AV1 in MP4 — yes, AVAssetWriter writes precompressed `av01`
each frame to a **dedicated serial encode queue** owning the encoder (libaom/libvpx encode
synchronously with internal lag; SVT is send/receive with its own threads). Encoded packets
go to the passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (MP4) or the WebM writer. Progress: frames
submitted (the encoder's lag, 25–35 frames, is under a second at 30 fps); a final flush
(`encode(NULL)` / SVT EOS) before `markAsFinished`. Cancel: the existing flag, checked per
frame by both pump and encode queue, then the encoder destroyed after `allInputsFinished`,
as G3c requires for the reader. Back-pressure is natural: the pump's
`isReadyForMoreMediaData` loop blocks on a bounded queue to the encoder.

Memory: one compositor frame is 16,588,800 B; I420 3,110,400 B; I010 6,220,800 B. Encoder
RSS measured above: SVT-AV1 1.0–2.1 GB at 1080p (most at preset 4 and 10-bit), libaom
0.5–1.1 GB, libvpx 0.3–0.5 GB. SVT's thread/buffer count follows `--lp`; 4K will be larger
(not measured).

### 7. HDR

| | HEVC rows today | AV1 | VP9 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Profile | Main 10 | Main (profile 0), 10-bit | Profile 2 |
| Colour in the bitstream | VUI | sequence header `color_config`: `AV1E_SET_COLOR_PRIMARIES/TRANSFER_CHARACTERISTICS/MATRIX_COEFFICIENTS` (libaom), `color_primaries`/`transfer_characteristics` in SVT's config — measured: aomenc `--transfer-characteristics=hlg` gave an MP4 ffprobe reads as `arib-std-b67` with no container tags | only `color_space` (BT.709/BT.2020…, `VP9E_SET_COLOR_SPACE`), **no transfer** — HLG/PQ must come from the container |
| MP4 tags | `colr` from `AVVideoColorPropertiesKey` | `colr` from the description's extensions — measured HLG and PQ | `vpcC` carries primaries/transfer/matrix — measured HLG |
| HDR10 metadata (HD-5's fixed values) | VT compression keys | `mdcv`/`clli` boxes from `MasteringDisplayColorVolume`/`ContentLightLevelInfo` extensions — measured written and read back; in-band metadata OBUs available (`aom_img_add_metadata` with `OBU_METADATA_TYPE_HDR_MDCV/CLL`, SVT `mastering_display`/`content_light_level`), not exercised; AV1-ISOBMFF says the boxes SHOULD be present and SHALL equal the OBUs | MP4 boxes as for AV1; WebM `Colour/MasteringMetadata` + `MaxCLL`/`MaxFALL` — measured with libwebm and read back by the core |
| WebM tags | — | `Colour` element — measured HLG | `Colour` element — measured PQ |

So the new 10-bit rows can take `hevc_10bit`'s place in H-3's rules (`"hdr": true`,
`dynamic_range` hlg/pq/sdr), with the tags written in both the bitstream (AV1) and the
container. No Dolby Vision question arises. Not measured: any player's HDR rendering of
these files.

- **#326 — An agent's `export` is a job in the Export Queue and answers at
  once; `export_status` follows it and `cancel_export` stops it.** (Amends
  AI-16.) Every refusal `export` had stays synchronous — the arguments, the
  core's settings, the folder — and so does the graphics gate
  (`Exporter.graphicsRefusal`, its "The export was not started: …"), run in
  the handler before anything is queued, so a call that could only fail
  enqueues nothing. Then the handler pauses the editor's playback and
  enqueues in `ExportQueueController.shared` exactly as Add to Queue does
  (the queue captures the media URLs, the reverse resolution and the
  graphics itself), and answers `{export_id, path, status}`, nothing else.
  The status words are the queue's states in the agent's spelling:
  `queued` (waiting), `running`, `done` (completed), `failed`,
  `cancelled`. `export_status {export_id}` never waits: it answers
  `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed` (seconds, three decimals,
  from the `export` handler's entry to now, or to the finish); `running`
  adds `progress` and the exporter's `phase` when it has one; `done` adds
  every key `export` answered before this (the settings used, `bytes` read
  at the finish, `burn_in_timecode`, `dynamic_range`, `loudness`,
  `graphic_warnings`); `failed` and `cancelled` add `reason`, the queue
  row's sentence. `cancel_export {export_id}` is the row's Cancel
  (`ExportQueueController.cancel`) for a queued or running job, answered as
  `export_status` answers then, and leaves a finished one alone. **The
  records live in memory for the launch** (`AgentExports`,
  `AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`), for ids `export` returned only — a
  person's own queued job is not reachable — and are copied from the queue
  inside its own change notification, synchronously on main, so a record
  outlives the row's Remove and Clear Finished; a record holds no project
  handle or graphic set. The Export Queue window is not opened for an agent
  export. The queue runs one job at a time, so an agent export waits
  behind a person's (`queued`), and the queue's quit question now covers an
  agent's export as it does a person's. Stop no longer reaches an export
  (AI-16 as amended): the call has already answered; a queued or running
  export stops by `cancel_export` or the Export Queue's Cancel. **Risk
  accepted:** an agent that never asks never learns the outcome, and the
  assistant cannot sleep between polls, so it asks again when its turn
  allows. `tools/proof/export_status_proof.py` (A1–A8, Z1) is the proof;
  every proof that expected the file on return follows the job through
  `MCP.export_with` in `tools/proof/mcp.py`, which returns an older build's
  blocking answer as it is.
- **#336 — A composition audio track none of whose segments has a source
  (missing media, a pending reverse, a pending ramp render) holds bundled

  (`tools/proof/missing_audio_proof.py --baseline`): with one audio track
  whose only clip's media file is missing, or whose reverse is pending, and

  "export: The operation could not be completed" (M1, M2, R1, R2), as did a
  missing `AV.mov` alone (V0); beside a track that sounds, both exports
  finished and matched that track alone (M3, M4, R3, R4). A composition
  audio track of nothing but empty edits is what the writer could not read.
  The silence is `app/Resources/Silence.caf`, 10 s of ALAC zeros at 48 kHz
  in two channels (spec §11 SY-23: an empty edit before a non-48 kHz segment
  is rate-converted wrongly, so the silence is 48 kHz), inserted back to back
  from 0 (`CompositionBuilder.fillSilence`, `CompositionBuilder+Silence.swift`)
  and never scaled, the last copy cut at the end. The track's id, its input
  parameters, its envelope, its onset (still nil, so no hold), its meter and

title:	Export AV1 and VP9, with bundled encoders (libaom/SVT-AV1, libvpx, libopus)
state:	OPEN
author:	kpgalligan
labels:	ai-drafted
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	377
--
Owner decision, 2026-10-27: Frame Job exports AV1 and VP9, with the encoders **bundled in the app**, not through a user-installed ffmpeg. "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."

## Why it needs bundling

Measured on an M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1, with `VTCopyVideoEncoderList`:
- VideoToolbox offers only these encoders: H.264, HEVC (also its alpha, depth and disparity variants), ProRes 422/4444/XQ, JPEG and H.263. There is no AV1 or VP9 encoder, and Apple's AV1 hardware on M3 and later decodes only.
- `VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported` is false for both AV1 and VP9 on this Mac.
- AVFoundation cannot write a WebM file.

Import already handles both formats: MP4 as is, WebM/Matroska through the built-in rewrap (#216, #227), and decode depends on the machine. Export does not.

## Scope, with the decisions still open

These go to a spike first, and the open choices come back to the owner:

- **AV1 encoder:** libaom (AOM's reference encoder, BSD-2 plus the AOM patent licence) or SVT-AV1 (BSD-3 plus the AOM patent licence). Measure speed and quality on Apple Silicon. rav1e (Rust) would break the "no pixel work in Rust" rule, so it needs the owner.
- **VP9 encoder:** libvpx (BSD-3), including VP9 with alpha in WebM. Chrome and Firefox play that as transparent web video; HEVC with alpha plays only in Safari.
- **Containers:**
  - AV1 in MP4: can `AVAssetWriter` write precompressed `av01` samples, or does it need a muxer of our own?
  - AV1 and VP9 in WebM: a Matroska *writer*. The core has only an index reader today.
- **Audio:** WebM carries Opus or Vorbis, not AAC, so that needs libopus (BSD-3). AV1-in-MP4 can keep AAC.
- **Depth and HDR:** 10-bit AV1, VP9 profile 2, HLG and PQ colour tags, to match the HEVC 10-bit and HDR rows.
- **Build:** each C library vendored or fetched at a pinned version, built for arm64 by the Makefile and Xcode, with provenance recorded. Their licences go in the acknowledgements (#376).
- **Speed:** software encodes run in the Export Queue. Measure 1080p30 throughput at the presets offered.

Owner decision, 2026-10-27: Frame Job exports AV1 and VP9, with the encoders **bundled in the app**, not through a user-installed ffmpeg. "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."

## Why it needs bundling

Measured on an M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1, with `VTCopyVideoEncoderList`:
- VideoToolbox offers only these encoders: H.264, HEVC (also its alpha, depth and disparity variants), ProRes 422/4444/XQ, JPEG and H.263. There is no AV1 or VP9 encoder, and Apple's AV1 hardware on M3 and later decodes only.
- `VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported` is false for both AV1 and VP9 on this Mac.
- AVFoundation cannot write a WebM file.

Import already handles both formats: MP4 as is, WebM/Matroska through the built-in rewrap (#216, #227), and decode depends on the machine. Export does not.

## Scope, with the decisions still open

These go to a spike first, and the open choices come back to the owner:

- **AV1 encoder:** libaom (AOM's reference encoder, BSD-2 plus the AOM patent licence) or SVT-AV1 (BSD-3 plus the AOM patent licence). Measure speed and quality on Apple Silicon. rav1e (Rust) would break the "no pixel work in Rust" rule, so it needs the owner.
- **VP9 encoder:** libvpx (BSD-3), including VP9 with alpha in WebM. Chrome and Firefox play that as transparent web video; HEVC with alpha plays only in Safari.
- **Containers:**
  - AV1 in MP4: can `AVAssetWriter` write precompressed `av01` samples, or does it need a muxer of our own?
  - AV1 and VP9 in WebM: a Matroska *writer*. The core has only an index reader today.
- **Audio:** WebM carries Opus or Vorbis, not AAC, so that needs libopus (BSD-3). AV1-in-MP4 can keep AAC.
- **Depth and HDR:** 10-bit AV1, VP9 profile 2, HLG and PQ colour tags, to match the HEVC 10-bit and HDR rows.
- **Build:** each C library vendored or fetched at a pinned version, built for arm64 by the Makefile and Xcode, with provenance recorded. Their licences go in the acknowledgements (#376).
- **Speed:** software encodes run in the Export Queue. Measure 1080p30 throughput at the presets offered.
- **Product surface:** new export preset rows (spec §7.8 and §6's `export` tool, so the MCP mirror and the guide's export page), plus dist_check rows proving the libraries are in the bundle and signed.

content.content:
### Risks

1. **Speed.** Software AV1 is 1.5–5.4× (SVT 8–4) slower than VideoToolbox HEVC per 1080p frame
   here (148–41 fps against ~222) and needs 1.0–2.1 GB; 4K is untested and will be ~4× the work. The sheet must say
   so (an estimate), and the Export Queue must not run two SVT jobs at once on a 16 GB Mac
   without measuring it.
2. **No AV1 decode on M1/M2**: Frame Job cannot preview or re-import its own AV1 export
   there (#216 refuses it), QuickTime won't play it, and proofs must check AV1 output with
   ffmpeg/dav1d. Only an M3+ can confirm playback (a manual-checks row).
3. **`av01` brand missing** from AVAssetWriter's `ftyp`; the in-place patch is a small byte
   rewrite after `finishWriting` that has to be right on every file (moov-first too).
4. **Rate accuracy**: 1-pass VBR undershot by up to 22 % on 5 s clips; an explicit
   `video_bitrate` will not be met exactly, and the "encoder decides" default needs an AV1
   rule (HEVC's 0.07 bpp is ~2× what SVT 6 needs for the same VMAF here).
5. **WebM is a second writer**, against §7.8's one-writer argument: chapters, range, size,
   the #337 audio length rule and graphic failures must hold there too.
6. **Alpha**: only Chrome/Firefox (Safari unconfirmed), ffmpeg's default VP9 decoder drops
   it, and Frame Job's own import drops VP9 alpha (#216-R) — an alpha WebM cannot come back
   in with its alpha.
7. **Build**: cmake on every build machine and the publish runner (runner not measured);
   perl from the OS; ~2 min clean build; network or a tarball cache for the sources.
8. **Licence duties**: BSD notices and the AOM patent licence text in the acknowledgements
   (#376); the AOM and Google grants terminate for a party that sues.
9. **VMAF caveats**: VMAF is not calibrated for HLG code values (`real8`/`real10`) and
   saturates on graphics (`promo`); clips are 5 s; HEVC was driven through ffmpeg rather than
   AVAssetWriter.
10. **WebM timing**: libwebm's default millisecond times and the reader's grid rule
    disagreed (grid false even with DefaultDuration, as for ffmpeg's WebM).

## C0 — decisions and the encoder build

### Record
  (the installed encoders, never committed);
- root Architecture: the encoders are platform-side (CX-4) — Swift calls SVT-AV1 and
  libvpx through the bridging header, no `rc_*` wraps them, and "no ffmpeg dependency"
  stands;
- `app/CLAUDE.md`: `CodecLibraries.swift` in the file map, and `main.swift`'s wiring
  (`CodecLibraries.probeIfAsked()` after `DecoderSupport.enable()`).

**Owed to later phases.** C1–C6 above; the acknowledgements file (#376), which lists
`Contents/Resources/Licenses/` and `vector.c`'s notice; a `published_check.py` row for
the codecs and an actions cache for `build/codecs` (neither in C0).

    threads at once: 150 frames each, every frame's 64RGBAHalf bytes equal (150 distinct
    frames), the I010 of frames 0, 75 and 149 byte-equal (691,200 bytes each), and 240,000

    and logged both readers at status 4 (cancelled) — on Debug.
  - **Mutants:** `audio-cancel-dropped` (the audio pump's own cancel gone) exit 1, `MUTANT
    CAUGHT`, F1–F3: each export still ended in time, but its audio reader was left reading

    with the readers' line not yet naming a shared reader, `CAUGHT, NOT EXACTLY` — F1 took

    woken the other read in those two runs. The readers' line then gained ` (one reader)` when

                "export",
                "Starts writing the timeline to a file and answers AT ONCE with "
                    + "{export_id, path, status} — ⌘E, the export sheet's six controls (format, "
                    + "size, frame rate, quality, loudness, range) in the sheet's own "
                    + "vocabulary, all but the frame rate — this exports at the document's "
                    + "rate, or on gif and apng at the format's own rate (12.5 and 25 fps). The "
                    + "export is a job in the Export Queue, run one at a time behind any other "
                    + "export already there; status is queued or running. Follow it with "
                    + "export_status, which never waits — call it again after a pause until "
                    + "status is done, failed or cancelled — and stop it with cancel_export. "
                    + "The export_id lasts until Frame Job quits. Every refusal comes back "
                    + "from this call, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing "
                    + "folder, and a graphic clip whose module does not compile; a failure "
                    + "while writing comes back from export_status, failed with its reason "
                    + "(a graphic that fails during the export stops it with no file left, "
                    + "naming the graphic and the frame). The preset is the ENCODING only and "
                    + "the size a separate choice defaulting to the document's own, or on gif "
                    + "and apng to the format's cap; the core resolves both into concrete "
                    + "settings (container, codec, size, rate, range) and hands them to the "
                    + "same exporter the sheet uses, so an agent export and a menu export "
                    + "cannot disagree. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the "
                    + "container's extension is added when the path has none. In an HLG "
                    + "project (set_canvas output) hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, "
                    + "prores_422 and prores_4444 write HLG unless dynamic_range says pq or sdr, and every "
                    + "other video preset writes the project's SDR version. What the finished "
                    + "file holds is export_status's done answer.",
                [
                    "preset": exportPresetProperty,
                    "path": [
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Where to write, e.g. ~/Movies/cut.mp4. The folder must "
                            + "exist.",
                    ],
                    "size": exportSizeProperty,
                    "range": [
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": ["project", "in_out"],
                        "description": "What to write: the whole timeline (default), or just "
                            + "the in/out range set_range set — the sheet's Range popup.",
                    ],
                    "video_bitrate": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "Target video rate in BITS per second (8000000 is "
                            + "8 Mbps) — the sheet's Quality popup. Omit to let the preset's "
                            + "own encoder settings decide. Ignored by presets that carry no "
                            + "rate of their own: ProRes is fixed by its profile, and GIF and "
                            + "APNG have no bitrate at all. On av1 and av1_webm it is a soft "
                            + "cap: SVT-AV1 "
                            + "encodes at a constant quality matched to HEVC at this rate (HEVC's "
                            + "0.07 bits per pixel per frame when omitted), and the file usually "
                            + "stays under it; very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 "
                            + "times over. On vp9_webm it is a soft cap too: libvpx encodes at a "
                            + "constant quality matched to HEVC at this rate (HEVC 10-bit's in an "
                            + "HDR export), and the file usually stays under it; up to about "
                            + "1.15 times it was measured.",
                    ],
                    "audio_bitrate": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "Target AAC or Opus rate in BITS per second (192000 "
                            + "is 192 kbps) — the sheet's Quality popup. Omit for 192 "
                            + "kbps. Ignored where the sound is neither: ProRes, WAV and AIFF "
                            + "all write LPCM, whose rate is its sample format.",
                    ],
                    "loudness_lufs": [
                        "type": "number", "minimum": -70, "maximum": 0,
                        "description": "Normalise the whole mix to this integrated loudness, "
                            + "in LUFS — the sheet's Loudness popup, whose rows are -14 "
                            + "(streaming), -16 (podcast) and -23 (EBU R 128 broadcast). The "
                            + "export measures itself first and then applies ONE gain to "
                            + "everything, so relative levels inside the timeline are "
                            + "untouched and no limiter is involved. Omit not to normalise: "
                            + "the export still measures and still reports. Ignored where "
                            + "there is no sound to measure (gif, apng).",
                    ],
                    "peak_dbtp": [
                        "type": "number", "minimum": -20, "maximum": 0,
                        "description": "The true-peak ceiling that gain is capped against, in "
                            + "dBTP. The sheet fixes it at -1 and this is the knob for "
                            + "anything else. Because normalisation is gain-only, a ceiling "
                            + "with no loudness_lufs beside it would have nothing to cap and "
                            + "is REFUSED rather than accepted and left inert. When the "
                            + "ceiling bites, the file lands quieter than the target asked "
                            + "for and the result's capped_by_peak says so.",
                    ],
                    "burn_in_timecode": burnInProperty,
                    // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-5, HD-14).
                    "dynamic_range": [
                        "type": "string", "enum": ["hlg", "pq", "sdr"],
                        "description": "An HDR (HLG) project's picture on hevc_10bit, av1, "
                            + "av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 and prores_4444 — the sheet's Dynamic "
                            + "Range popup: hlg (the default; BT.2100 HLG, no Dolby Vision), pq (HDR10: "
                            + "BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², mastering display P3-D65 0.005–1,000 "
                            + "cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000, MaxFALL 0) or sdr (the SDR version). Every "
                            + "other video preset writes the SDR version; hlg and pq are refused "
                            + "there and in an SDR project, where sdr changes nothing.",
                    ],
                    // The sheet's Speed popup (spec §11 CX-2, CX-12 (2)).
                    "encoder_speed": [
                        "type": "string", "enum": ["faster", "balanced", "smaller"],
                        "description": "av1's and av1_webm's encoder speed — the sheet's "
                            + "Speed popup: faster "
                            + "(SVT-AV1 preset 8), balanced (preset 6, the default) or smaller "
                            + "(preset 4, the smallest file for the picture and the slowest). "
                            + "Refused on every other preset, vp9_webm included (libvpx has one "
                            + "speed).",
                    ],
                ], required: ["preset", "path"]),
            // Window ▸ Export Queue's row for the job (spec §11 #326).
            tool(
                "export_status",
                "How an export this launch started is going — Window ▸ Export Queue's row "
                    + "for it, read now: it never waits, so call it again after a pause. "
                    + "Always export_id, status (queued, running, done, failed or "
                    + "cancelled), path and elapsed (seconds since export was called, or to "
                    + "the finish once it has finished). running adds progress (0 to 1) and "
                    + "phase while the exporter names one (the loudness measurement). done "
                    + "adds what the file holds: ok, bytes, the settings that were used "
                    + "(preset, container, codec, width, height, fps [num, den], start, "
                    + "duration), burn_in_timecode, dynamic_range in an HLG project (the "
                    + "picture written), encoder_speed on av1 and av1_webm, loudness for "
                    + "every format "
                    + "that carries sound, normalised or not — summary, integrated_lufs, "
                    + "true_peak_dbtp, "
                    + "sample_peak_dbfs, gain_db, ceiling_dbtp, capped_by_peak and target_lufs "
                    + "when one was asked, read off the mix that was written — and "
                    + "graphic_warnings [{name, frame, message}], each distinct warning a "
                    + "graphic gave while the file was drawn, absent when none. failed and "
                    + "cancelled add reason, the queue row's sentence. Only ids export "
                    + "returned are known, until Frame Job quits.",
                [
                    "export_id": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "The export_id export answered.",
                    ]
                ], required: ["export_id"]),
            // The Export Queue row's Cancel (spec §11 #326).
            tool(
                "cancel_export",
                "Stops an export this launch started — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A "
                    + "queued one is cancelled before it starts; a running one stops and "
                    + "its half-written file is removed, though the answer may still read "
                    + "running until the writer has stopped (export_status then reads "
                    + "cancelled). A finished one is left alone. Answers as export_status "
                    + "does.",
                [
                    "export_id": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "The export_id export answered.",
                    ]
                ], required: ["export_id"]),
        ]
    }
}

     320 docs/guide/export.md
3:Frame Job writes the timeline out as a movie, an audio file or an animated image, and saves single frames as stills. One export sheet covers every format. You choose the format, then the size, frame rate, quality, loudness and range, and the sheet shows what the file will be before anything is written. Exports can run at once behind a progress sheet, or wait in the Export Queue while you keep editing. Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured.
11:The sheet reopens on the **last choices you exported with**. Clicking **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them; Cancel does not. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.
24:| **Speed** | How long the AV1 encoder works on each frame. See [Speed](#speed). | Balanced |
35:- **Footnote:** the codec, the container (left out when it is the same word, as in `GIF`), the AV1 speed (`AV1 · MP4 · Balanced`, `AV1 · WEBM · Balanced`; VP9 has none: `VP9 · WEBM`), the video rate, the audio rate (`192 kbps audio`), the loudness target (`−14 LUFS`) and `alpha` when the format keeps transparency. When you pick a Quality tier and the format sets its own rate, it reads `format's own rate` instead of a number.
47:| AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | The smallest delivery file, encoded by the AV1 encoder built into Frame Job. 10-bit, and it can carry HDR. Slower to export than HEVC. See [Speed](#speed). |
48:| AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | The same AV1 picture in a WebM file, with Opus sound, for the web. Frame Job writes the WebM itself. |
49:| VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | VP9 in a WebM file, with Opus sound: the web format every browser plays, encoded by the VP9 encoder built into Frame Job. 8-bit, or 10-bit when it carries HDR. Slower to export than HEVC and larger than AV1 for the same picture. |
58:Sound in the movie formats is stereo at 48 kHz: AAC in H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha and AV1 (MP4), Opus in AV1 (WebM) and VP9 (WebM), and 16-bit LPCM in both ProRes formats. A project with no sound exports a WebM with no sound track. GIF and APNG carry no sound. A file's sound is exactly as long as the range it exports, including when a clip in it plays faster or slower.
75:- **Even dimensions.** H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats, VP9 (WebM) and ProRes 422 need them, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. ProRes 4444, GIF and APNG keep an odd edge.
82:### Speed
84:The **Speed** row sits under Format (under Dynamic Range in an HDR project). It is live only on **AV1 (MP4)** and **AV1 (WebM)**; on every other format it is greyed out and keeps your last choice. **VP9 (WebM)** has one speed, so the row is greyed out there too.
88:| **Faster** | The quickest AV1 export, a slightly larger file for the same picture. |
90:| **Smaller file** | The slowest AV1 export, the smallest file for the same picture. |
92:AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, so they take longer than the HEVC formats, which use the Mac's hardware encoder. The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in presets.
113:- HEVC formats, AV1 and VP9 ask for 60 % of the H.264 rate. AV1's and VP9's **Format default** is the HEVC rate too.
114:- For **AV1** the rate is a soft cap. AV1 encodes at a constant quality chosen to match or beat HEVC at that rate, so it usually stays under the rate and simple footage comes out much smaller. Very detailed footage can go over: up to about 1.25 times the rate was measured. Its tier titles and footnote read `usually ≤ …`.
115:- For **VP9 (WebM)** the rate is a soft cap the same way: VP9 encodes at a constant quality chosen to match or beat HEVC at that rate (HEVC 10-bit's in an HDR export), and the file usually stays under it. Up to about 1.15 times the rate was measured. Its tier titles and footnote read `usually ≤ …` too.
176:- **Add to Queue** opens the same save panel, then puts the job in the Export Queue so you can keep editing.
200:## The Export Queue
202:**Window ▸ Export Queue** lists queued exports. It opens on its own whenever you click **Add to Queue**.
211:- With nothing queued, the window says so: "Nothing queued. The Export card's Add to Queue button puts a confirmed export here instead of waiting for it, and they run one at a time while you keep editing."
213:Closing the window stops nothing. Opening the export sheet pauses playback whichever button you use, but after **Add to Queue** there is no progress sheet in the way: you can resume playback and keep editing while the job runs.
215:Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first: "An export is still being written." The message names the running file and counts the jobs still waiting ("“*name*” is not finished, and 2 more are waiting."). **Quit Anyway** cancels the queue and deletes the partly written file. This question comes after Frame Job has asked about unsaved documents.
217:Only queued exports are protected this way. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing does not ask, and the half-written file is left behind. Cancel that export first.
236:- A frame showing a deep still or a 10-bit VP9 clip is saved as a 16-bit PNG or 10-bit HEIC. JPEG is always 8-bit.
255:Only HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats, VP9 (WebM), ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 can carry HDR. VP9 (WebM) is 10-bit (VP9 Profile 2) for HLG and HDR10, and 8-bit (Profile 0, which every player decodes) for the SDR version. On every other video format the row is greyed out on **SDR version**, which is what those formats write. What each choice contains, and how the SDR version is made, is in [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md#exporting-hdr).
272:- **Speed ramps and Keep pitch off.** An export waits for the rendered audio of every speed ramp, and of every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, to finish before it writes, and shows "Preparing…" meanwhile. That sound is never exported silent (see [Speed](speed.md)). If it cannot be rendered, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …".
279:`export` mirrors **Export…** with **Add to Queue**: it checks the request, puts the job in the Export Queue and answers at once with `{export_id, path, status}`. Status is `queued` or `running`.
283:| `preset` (required) | Format | `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif`, `apng`. |
287:| `video_bitrate`, `audio_bitrate` | Quality | Bits per second. On `av1`, `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, `video_bitrate` is a soft cap the file usually stays under. `audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate. |
292:| `encoder_speed` | Speed | `faster`, `balanced` (default) or `smaller`. `av1` and `av1_webm` only; refused on every other format, `vp9_webm` included. |
296:Every refusal comes back from `export` itself, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline, or a graphic that does not compile.
298:- `export_status {export_id}` answers the job's row without waiting: `queued`, `running` (with `progress` from 0 to 1 and `phase`), `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Call it again after a pause until the job finishes.
300:  - `done` adds `bytes`, the settings the file was written with, `burn_in_timecode`, `dynamic_range` in an HLG project, `encoder_speed` for AV1 and AV1 (WebM), any `graphic_warnings` and, for every format with sound, `loudness`: `summary`, `integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `sample_peak_dbfs`, `gain_db`, `ceiling_dbtp`, `capped_by_peak` and `target_lufs`.
301:  - `failed` and `cancelled` add `reason`, the queue row's sentence.
316:- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
317:- AV1's and VP9's file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1 and about 1.15 times with VP9.
319:- Queued jobs run one at a time. **Export…** does not join the queue: it writes straight away, behind its own progress sheet.
320:- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Issue batch B57 (#210): which `beginSheetModal(for:)` sites can be asked
for while another sheet is attached to the editor window, and whether the
document's alert queue keeps their order, measured through the app's own
sources.

    python3 tools/proof/sheet_queue_probe.py [--sources DIR] [--mutant NAME] [--only IDS]

`sheet_queue_probe.swift` is built with `swift_build.py`'s line over
`--sources` and run once, in a process of its own, under
`tools/proof/work/sheet-queue/<tree|mutant-NAME>/`, killed at a 240 s wall.
Prints `<ID> pass|fail — <detail>` per row, then `scores: N/M`.

The fixture is an untitled document whose `EditorViewController` is the
content of a 1440×900 window owned by the document's window controller. E1
and E2 are `present(_:)` of "probe alert one" and "probe alert two"; an
attached sheet is ended 0.3 s after it attaches unless a row holds it.

Rows:
  B0   the probe builds.
  C0   CONTROL: `windowForSheet` is the window, no sheet is attached, and
       `addMediaFiles:` validates true.

and append, and the end of stream drained before `markAsFinished`. SVT-AV1
runs capped CRF (CX-13): the cap is `video_bitrate`, or HEVC's 0.07 bits
per pixel per frame when none is asked, set as `max_bit_rate`, and the CRF
is the one CX-13's calibration gives the speed at the cap's bits per pixel
per frame — matching or beating HEVC at that rate. The cap is soft (SVT's
default 50 % overshoot): a file usually averages far less than the rate,
and detailed footage was measured up to 1.254 × it; with a closed GOP and a
keyframe at least every 2 s (`intra_period_length` = ⌊2·fps⌋ − 1), and writes the

container bytes are the core's (`rc_av1_*`, CX-12 (4)): the `av1C` record

stripped, and the finished file's `ftyp` rewritten in place so `av01` is a
compatible brand (`isom mp41 mp42` → `isom av01 mp42`); a file whose `ftyp`
cannot take it fails the export. The packets go to a passthrough

colour tags (the `colr` box), one sample each; on `pq` alone HD-5's fixed HDR10
metadata is written twice, as SVT-AV1's HDR_MDCV and HDR_CLL metadata OBUs on

the file will have — a vertical 1080 × 1920 timeline's "GIF default" is
152 × 270 — and `ExporterImageSequence` draws each frame at exactly that

under a queued job, cannot change what the file draws. Before the build it

clip of each nest reached from a clip in the range, however deep, whose
module did not compile
or is not in `graphics/` refuses the export before anything is written,
each named with its first diagnostic. Nothing is gated for an audio-only

# Spec §11 — decisions: Codec export (road map "codec-export", #377)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that makes these is `designs/codec-export.md` (in progress); its spike record
(`## S — the spike`) holds every measurement cited here. CX-1..CX-11 were recorded in C0,
before any code. Each is marked "owner" (the owner's choice, 2026-10-27) or "default" (the
orchestrator's default, which the owner can still change by a new entry here).

  "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."). Frame Job exports AV1 and VP9 with
  encoders built into the app, as four rows:
  1. AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
  2. AV1 in WebM, with Opus audio;
  3. VP9 in WebM, with Opus audio;
  4. VP9 with alpha in WebM.

  VP9 in MP4 is not wanted: it works (the spike measured it) but carries no alpha and is less
  efficient than AV1 in MP4, so it does nothing another row does not. AV1 with alpha is not
  wanted because none exists in practice: neither SVT-AV1's nor libaom's API takes an alpha
  input, and the Matroska AV1 mapping defines none. **Risk accepted:** software encoding is
  1.5–5.4× slower than VideoToolbox's HEVC per 1080p frame on the spike's M2 Max and needs
  1.0–2.1 GB, and the app grows by about 5 MB.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Road map 2, phase 7 (Output) — the OFFSCREEN half of the proof.

**Almost nothing in phase 7 can be photographed, and that is a fact about the
features rather than about the harness.** Save Frame is a save panel; the
export sheet is a sheet; the export queue is a window of its own. The harness
renders an `EditorViewController`'s content view into a PNG — a panel is not in
it, a sheet is not in it, a second window is not in it, and no sheet can be put
up offscreen at all (which is why phase 3's Remove Silences candidates arrive as
a harness ARGUMENT rather than as a photograph of its sheet). So this script is
mostly PROBES, which is the route `phase6_chrome.py` took for the Clip menu and
`phase5_chrome.py` took for `Loudness`: a `main.swift` of its own compiled
against the WHOLE of `app/Sources` with `swift_build.py`'s line,
cached by content, and scored as a FAILURE rather than an exit when
it will not build, so a rotted instrument cannot take the rest of the run down.

What is claimed, section by section:

    1  **the menu and the validator.** File ▸ Save Frame… exists, carries
       `saveFrame:`, and takes ⌥⌘E — the letter Export… already has, under
       two modifiers rather than one, measured as flags read off `NSEvent`
       rather than as a number written here. Window ▸ Export Queue exists,
       carries `showExportQueue:` and takes no key equivalent at all. Then
       `validateSaveFrameAction`: **false on a zero-duration project and true
       on one with a clip**, and `nil` for a selector that is not its own —
       the arm is load-bearing, and a build whose arm answered `true`
       unconditionally would offer a command that can only open a panel and
       then apologise.
    2  **`FrameWriter`, called directly.** Three formats and their whole
       vocabulary; `format(for:requested:)` over every spelling that matters,
       including that `heif` is NOT one of them; three files written from one

### Fix pass 1 (2026-10-28): the rebase onto main and the review's nits

**The rebase.** The review passed with four nits. C4 then became one commit on `codecs`, rebased
onto main `d0f9fe0`, which brought:
- `ef3414f`, the release items (PUB-10..PUB-12, `published_check` P22–P25, the codecs cache);
- `d0f9fe0`, #378: `ExportWriter` reads through one `AVAssetReader` per output, and a block

The code merged with no conflict. C4's one line in `ExporterWriter.swift` is
